hypothesis: Learned joint rate variation plus count noise improves under-dispersed prop probabilities while preserving the incumbent game forecast and improved joint rotation minutes.

protocol.rateTraining: Earlier seasons only; earlier-game rate estimates with 24-hour result embargo; observed target minutes used only as exposure in conditional rate-residual training, never supplied to a forecast
protocol.meanModel: Existing earlier-season player rate estimator and joint-rotation minute model
protocol.countModel: Method-of-moments Poisson-lognormal joint rate covariance, diagonal Poisson component removed, off-diagonals shrunk only when required for positive definiteness; global learned rebound/assist rate correction
protocol.gameModel: Exact linked incumbent team-score draws; no candidate rotation impact added to those scores
protocol.playerPoints: Multinomial allocation of the incumbent team score using sampled minutes and correlated scoring-rate weights; inactive players get zero
protocol.playerReboundsAssists: Poisson counts with learned correlated lognormal rate variation
protocol.evaluationRoster: Previous listed roster proxy, same player identities and same 60 deterministically selected games from the previously inspected replay sample
protocol.thresholds: Fixed diagnostic thresholds; not historical Sportsbet main lines or a profitability test
protocol.promotion: No automatic promotion. Require same-case point-error non-regression, minute MAE at most 4.5, distribution reliability by market family and independent forward evidence.

limitations: Historical seasons have already been inspected; these results are development evidence, not a fresh validation set.
Roster proxies are incomplete and lack verified point-in-time injury or transaction reconstruction.
Discrete count ranges can cover more than their nominal probability; broader intervals alone are not an accuracy improvement.
No model changes are fitted to the user's recent 19-game live sample.
Live player props remain uncalibrated and Low confidence.
